thread.title: Senator Rick Scott introduces bill to increase SNAP fraud reporting requirements
thread.title_full: Senator Rick Scott introduces bill to increase SNAP fraud reporting requirements

author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Senator Rick Scott introduces bill to increase SNAP fraud reporting requirements
text:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott introduced the SNAP Fraud Reporting Act on June 10, aiming to reduce fraud within federal programs and protect American taxpayers.
The proposed legislation would require states to submit comprehensive data on fraud in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which would then compile a national report for Congress. According to Scott, “We cannot tolerate fraud because it steals from the Americans who need these programs the most. As elected officials, we have a responsibility to taxpayers to make sure every dollar is spent wisely, fairly, and in compliance with federal law. That’s both a constitutional and a moral responsibility we have to the American people. By passing this legislation, we will create a pathway to identify and crack down on fraud so taxpayers don’t get ripped off.”
Representative Dave Taylor of Ohio first introduced similar legislation in the House of Representatives. Taylor said, “Hardworking American families deserve access to the benefits they’ve earned during times of need, not having them siphoned away by fraudsters chasing a quick payday. With the fraud we’ve seen running rampant across federal programs, there’s never been a more critical time for accountability. I’m pleased to see Senator Rick Scott lead the effort in the Senate to advance greater transparency, protect SNAP benefits for vulnerable Buckeyes who rely on them, and ensure USDA has the tools to hold states accountable for the proper use of taxpayer dollars.”
In February 2025, Secretary Rollins at USDA directed states to share SNAP data for program integrity verification; however, 21 states refused and filed lawsuits against this directive. In November 2025, initial data from 29 cooperating states revealed that nearly 200,000 individuals receiving SNAP benefits were associated with deceased individuals’ Social Security numbers.
The act seeks an amendment of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 mandating state submission of SNAP fraud data.
Scott champions fiscal responsibility as well as policies supporting families and small businesses; he served in active duty aboard USS Glover after high school; he won election representing Florida in the U.S. Senate; he holds degrees from University of Missouri-Kansas City and Southern Methodist University; he serves on several Senate committees including Armed Services and Budget; together with his wife Ann they raised two daughters—all according to his official website.
